the_experiment_stated_before_it_runs.H_what_is_being_tested: Part II §2 of today's record derives, programmatically over every row in analytics/fetch-results/, that https://icsid.worldbank.org/cases/content/tables-of-decisions/manifest-lack-of-legal-merit has returned THREE distinct page states on THREE consecutive observation dates, each exactly one byte shorter than the last and each CONSTANT WITHIN ITS DATE: 94,996 / 66a879e013bd (2026-08-19, 5 rows), 94,995 / 29bd0911889f (2026-08-20, 6 rows), 94,994 / ebcebcae8594 (2026-08-21, 2 rows). BUT WITHIN-DATE CONSTANCY HAS ONLY EVER BEEN OBSERVED WITHIN A SINGLE RUN, where the rows are seconds apart. That is a weak test of intra-day stability and this batch is an honest attempt to strengthen it.
the_experiment_stated_before_it_runs.the_two_branches_fixed_now_so_neither_ca: BRANCH A - urls[2] returns bytes 94994 AND sha256 ebcebcae859452373dedf300a3bcaa833d2c37ee4bbaf3c466782b8653bc5981. Then the page was byte-identical across the interval between the two runs, the drift is at coarser-than-this-interval granularity, and a DAILY digest comparison remains mechanically conceivable. BRANCH B - urls[2] returns any other digest. Then the page changes WITHIN a day, the drift is continuous or near-continuous, and NO digest comparison at ANY granularity can signal that this table's CONTENTS changed. BOTH BRANCHES SUPPORT THE SAME CONSERVATIVE CONCLUSION already drawn in Part II §2 - that a digest change on this URL is not evidence the table changed - and this batch can only sharpen the mechanism, never rescue the signal.
the_experiment_stated_before_it_runs.the_limit_I_state_before_the_answer_rath: THE INTERVAL IS SHORT AND I WILL NOT DRESS IT UP. The morning run was 2026-08-21T11:20:56Z; this batch runs whenever the runner picks it up, tens of minutes later at best. BRANCH A THEREFORE LICENSES ONLY 'byte-identical across an interval of roughly this length', WITH THE ACTUAL INTERVAL COMPUTED FROM THE TWO fetched_at VALUES AND STATED - it does NOT license 'stable across the day', and per G4 no duration may be read off fetched_at for any other purpose. BRANCH B is the strong branch: a single differing digest falsifies within-day constancy outright, and it needs no interval argument at all.
the_experiment_stated_before_it_runs.why_this_is_worth_a_batch_at_all: This council was building toward a sha256 change-detector on exactly this page as a signal that ICSID's register had been updated - it is a live proposal on the operator's PENDING list. A signal that fires every day regardless of content is worse than no signal, because a seat will read a firing as news. Establishing the drift's granularity is what tells the operator whether the proposal is salvageable at daily granularity or dead outright.
